title: Trumpet
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS Bb trumpet (Bach 180S37 Stradivarius, 1987, per MISBbtrumpet.html)
summary: A Bb trumpet with the valves up, played by a lip valve whose pitch is never an input: the note is the lock the loop finds between the lip and the bore, and only the open harmonics of the instrument are valid. The bore is the 34-station profile (mouthpiece cup and throat, backbore, leadpipe, cylinder, bell) published with Tournemenne and Chabassier (2019), copied digit for digit from the openwind example file; its valves are straightened, so the valve loops, slides and ports are absent. The lip is the outward-striking mode of the artificial latex lips Cullen (2000) measured on a trombone-size mouthpiece (her embouchure 19, the tightest of 20), because no trumpeter's lip is published; it is a trombone-rig artificial lip, not a trumpeter's, and playability entered the choice (the looser embouchure 7 the trombone uses would not start D5 below 27.5 kPa nor hold it below about 21 kPa). The graded sound is the radiated pressure of the actual bell disk at a baffled point 1.524 m away, not the mouthpiece pressure. Nothing was fitted to the Iowa recordings; the pre-stress of each held note was set from the emergent pitch of a first render against equal temperament (a player tuning an embouchure), and no pitch, note or frequency is an input. It is a population stand-in (a different trumpet from the recorded Bach 180S37), and that the stations were measured from a real commercial trumpet is as reported and not verified by this lane.
physics_present: fs-couple brass_loop: a one-degree-of-freedom outward-striking lip island advanced by exact held-force propagation, a Bernoulli aperture solved implicitly with the mouthpiece junction, closing on the bore's reflectance

fs-duct multimodal transfer-matrix bore with exact Bessel viscothermal loss, realized as a passive causal line by a convergence ladder over the line length, terminated in the flanged-piston radiation load; the mouthpiece cup and throat are geometry in the bore, not a lumped volume

an outlet observer built from the same duct: the mouth volume flow per incident wave from the same transfer-matrix chain, differentiated and delayed by the Rayleigh integral over the real 0.061 m bell disk to a baffled receiver, so the graded sound is radiated pressure, not mouthpiece pressure

a lip tension gesture (pre-stress) and a blowing-pressure gesture on the shared canonical schedule format, with held-note, tension-sweep and pressure-ramp recipes in render.sh (the ramps measure the oscillation threshold, extinction pressure and hysteresis of this model)

diagnostic taps in music_render lip, none of them an input to a note: --impedance scans the passive bore (multimodal and plane-wave input impedance peaks and heights, and the analytic radiated-per-internal transfer of a baffled piston on axis), --mouthpiece-wav writes the internal mouthpiece pressure, and the sidecar carries per-0.1 s lip-closure and mouthpiece-level windows; the observer chain was checked against that analytic transfer and agrees to 1.2 dB through partial 8 on F4, so the radiation path is not where the spectrum is lost
physics_missing: the valves: the bore file is straightened, so the valve loops, tuning slide, valve slides and ports are absent, and only the open-valve harmonic series (concert Bb3, F4, Bb4, D5) is valid; valve combinations are not rendered

the recorded trumpet: the Iowa instrument is a Bach 180S37 and no numeric bore of it was found, so this is a population stand-in; the measured-from-a-real-trumpet origin of the stations is as reported, the paper text could not be opened (HAL bot challenge) and the file states no maker, method or uncertainty

a trumpet player's lips: the lip is an artificial latex lip pair measured on a trombone-size mouthpiece (cup 25.5 mm against this trumpet's 16.8 mm), only its outward-striking mode, with a channel width and rest gap that are not a trumpeter's; no trumpet-player lip mass, width or rest gap is published (Yoshikawa 1995, Richards 2003 and the Stevenson and Campbell work were looked for and none gives a complete set). Embouchure 19 was chosen over 7 for the cup diameter (7's 12 mm channel is 47 percent of the rig cup but 71 percent of this one) and because playability entered the choice: D5 on embouchure 7 started only at 27.5 kPa and stopped near 20.8 kPa, so a 21 kPa hold fell silent, because a single loose lip row scaled only by pre-stress puts every upper note at the extinction edge, and not because the lip resonance missed the bore mode (diagnostic sweeps speak the Bb4 and D5 windows on embouchure 7 at 25 kPa)

intonation: the stand-in bore's own passive impedance peaks lie 41 to 62 cents flat of the equal-tempered open series for partials 3 to 6, so the notes are flat of equal temperament until the lip is tightened, and the hold pre-stresses (0.93, 1.42, 1.9, 2.42) were chosen to bring the emergent pitch to the note; how a real Bach 180S37 would sit is unknown

the level and the spectrum of the source (diagnostic, measured on the embouchure-19 holds at 14 kPa): the mouthpiece pressure is 173 to 176 dB rms (re 20 uPa) against 166.9 to 167.2 dB at the shank of a trumpet played forte (Resch et al., arXiv 1611.01025), 6 to 9 dB too high with the blowing pressure at the top of Bouhuys's 4 to 13 kPa; the lip closes in 87 to 97 percent of the 0.1 s chunks; the passive impedance peaks are not too high against the one published calculated pair (no missing-loss evidence); and the internal spectrum falls steeply (F4: partials 2 to 7 at -12, -14, -22, -26, -35, -41 dB re the fundamental), 22 to 24 dB steeper at partial 4 than the recordings imply once the measured bore-to-radiation transfer is allowed for, so the radiated spectral centroid stays far below the Iowa notes. Nonlinear propagation is absent and is the leading unproven candidate: at these amplitudes the shock-formation distance (about 0.7 to 1.1 m by the standard estimate) is shorter than the tube
the mouthpiece as a separate measured part: the cup and throat come from the same station table, and their agreement with a Bach 7C or any named mouthpiece is not established

a clock that reaches the bell's radiation ceiling: the flanged radiation load is admitted only to ka 20, so the render runs on a 32 kHz clock (not 48 kHz) and everything above the receiver's resolved band (6.9 kHz) is unmodelled

the mouth-flow radiation transfer is the plane-mode image of the duct, not the multimodal one the reflectance line uses; and the microphone is an on-axis point: the player's bell orientation, the cardioid KM 84 directivity and any room are not modelled
breath-warmed and humidified bore gas, wall vibration, nonlinear propagation and shock formation at forte (the source of brassiness), mutes, and the player's tonguing and vibrato
a same-specimen or same-model impedance pair, so the passive chain is checked only against published population data
